title: WHAT IF YOUR TELESCOPE SAW 100X MORE SKY?

segments.line: You hold a camera that sees one hundred Hubbles at once.
Hubble sees this tiny square. Roman sees all of this.
Same two point four metre mirror.
The trick is three mirrors, and a focal length a third as long.
It sees in infrared, like Webb's cousin.
Hubble spent ten years stitching Andromeda.
Roman does it in a few clicks.
NASA says nearly fifteen hundred times faster.
Hubble has seen one tenth of one percent of the sky.
Roman will image fifty times that in five years.
Its first pictures drop on seventh December.
You can even claim one pixel.
It's named for NASA's first chief astronomer.
Tomorrow: what if the Sun blinked out for one minute?
One hundred Hubbles in one shot. Full film on the channel.
